name: AD823 (dual 16 MHz JFET-input, rail-to-rail output) + AD823A (2012 XFCB redesign)
tagline: ADI's 1995 JFET-input, rail-to-rail-output dual that runs from 3 V. A CMoy/portable-amp favourite; Tangent rated it punchier in the bass and more detailed than OPA132/134.
technology: Original AD823: N-channel JFET input stage on ADI's complementary bipolar (CB) process (PNP/NPN fT 600-800 MHz). Nested-integrator topology with Miller compensation and a complementary common-emitter rail-to-rail output stage. Offset and drift are thin-film trimmed. Input range extends 0.2 V below -Vs, with no phase inversion at the rails. Supply 3-36 V single or ±1.5 to ±18 V. ADI PCN 26_0029 (2026) moves the listed AD823 order codes to ADI's Camas, WA wafer fab, with no datasheet change. AD823A (2012) is a different die with the same dual pinout: XFCB process (dielectrically isolated complementary bipolar with JFETs and thin-film resistors), two-stage design with a folded-cascode first stage, laser-trimmed, rail-to-rail output.

reputation.summary: A 2000s DIY headphone-amp favourite for battery-powered CMoy-style portables. Tangent (tangentsoft; also in Soomal's Chinese translation) rated it a bit punchier in the bass and more detailed than the OPA134/132. He considered it ideal for battery amps because it runs on 3 V with a rail-to-rail output, but warned it can be too aggressive with already forward headphones and that its roughly 15 mA output is low. Soomal says the AD823 'is also considered' warm with good dynamics; that is general reputation, not a Soomal listening test. Soomal reports that earlier Graham Slee SOLO versions used it, and it appears in the Colorfly C4 Pro and Hidizs AP100 DAPs (its role in the AP100 is unclear). No independent audio measurements (ASR, Samuel Groner) were checked.
sonic_descriptors: warm (偏暖; Soomal, citing general reputation)
'emotional', good with acoustic music (Head-Fi, per discovery notes; thread not verified)
typical_uses: Battery-powered CMoy / portable headphone amps (3 V single supply, rail-to-rail output)
Graham Slee SOLO headphone amp, earlier versions per Soomal
DAP analog stage: Colorfly C4 Pro (Soomal teardown); Hidizs AP100 (Soomal teardown; role unconfirmed, either output filter or headphone driver)
Op-amp rolling in DIY and commercial DAC/amps
ADI's own 3 V stereo headphone-driver application circuit
caveats: Low output current: 15-17 mA linear, rated 0.5 V from the rails. Weak for low-impedance headphones without a buffer (Tangent).
Offset is much higher on ±15 V (3.5 mV max vs 0.8 mV at 5 V).
Input overvoltage: if an input can exceed +VS by more than 300 mV, or signal is applied with the supplies off, use a series resistor (1 kΩ withstands 10 V continuous).
About 20° phase margin driving 470 pF as a follower; add a series output resistor for capacitive loads.
PDIP exists only as the original AD823ANZ. The AD823A redesign is SOIC/MSOP only.
New stock after PCN 26_0029 (2026) comes from a different wafer fab (Camas, WA). ADI states no fit/form/function change, but old and new stock are not guaranteed to be identical silicon.
Can sound too aggressive with already forward headphones (Tangent).
Reputation evidence is mostly subjective (Tangent, Chinese reviews, Head-Fi).

revision_history.changes: Changes to Specifications and Ordering Guide; updated Outline Dimensions. Pb-free AD823ARZ/-RL/-R7 added ('Z = Pb-free part') alongside AD823AN and AR/-REEL/-REEL7. Abs-max differential input was ±1.2 V. The ±15 V table had unit errors (Ib at TMAX in pA, Ios in nA).
Updated format. Changes to DC Performance (p.5), Outline Dimensions and Ordering Guide. The ±15 V unit fixes are attributed here only by inference.
Changes to Table 4 (Absolute Maximum Ratings). The A-to-E difference in differential input (±1.2 V to ±VS) is attributed here by inference.
Changes to Figure 34 (pulse response, CL = 470 pF) and Figure 36 (simplified schematic).

Editorial changes to Theory of Operation and changes to the Ordering Guide, which lists AD823ANZ, AR/-REEL/-REEL7, ARZ/-RL/-R7 and AD823AR-EBZ; AD823AN is not listed. No electrical spec change. Still the current revision in 2026, including after PCN 26_0029.
Initial version of the AD823A (new XFCB part).
Added an Absolute Maximum Ratings caution about overheating from output current at a 30 V supply. Changes to Equation 8.

silicon_changes.summary: ADI PCN 26_0029, 'Qualification of ADI Camas Wafer Fab CB Processes', moves Complementary Bipolar production to 'the existing qualified process at the Analog Devices Camas, WA Fab to ensure a reliable and continuous supply', with 'no expected impact to fit, form, function or reliability'. A web-search summary lists AD823ANZ and AD823ARZ among the affected parts. The part number stays the same while the fab changes. No die-layout change is stated.

silicon_changes.audio_impact: Unknown. ADI claims no change to fit, form or function, and the data-sheet limits are unchanged. No listening or measurement comparisons of stock made before and after the transfer exist. Anyone who prizes older AD823ANZ stock should record date codes.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low - ADI states no fit/form/function impact and the data sheet is unchanged. The risk matters mainly for matched pairs or comparisons of old and new stock.

silicon_changes.when: 2012 (AD823A data sheet Rev. A 5/12, Rev. B 6/12)
silicon_changes.identification: A separate part, 'AD823A', with double-A order codes (AD823AARZ, versus the original AD823ARZ). Offered in SOIC_N and MSOP only; MSOP branding is H34. Its data sheet is D09439, 'Wide Supply Dual, 17 MHz...'; the original's is D00901, 'Dual, 16 MHz...'. Beware: the original AD823 data sheet labels its A-grade column 'AD823A', and the original SOIC codes are AD823AR/ARZ, so a listing that says only 'AD823A' is ambiguous. Differences in SOIC top marking are unverified.
silicon_changes.summary: ADI created a materially different die under a near-identical name, and it sits alongside the original rather than replacing it. The AD823A uses the XFCB dielectrically isolated complementary-bipolar process with a two-stage folded-cascode design. The original AD823 uses the CB process with a nested integrator. Revisions 0 to E of the original AD823 data sheet show only editorial, abs-max, figure and ordering changes. Pinout and supply range match, but specs, output drive and packages differ.

silicon_changes.audio_impact: No listening or measurement reports on the AD823A were found. On paper it fixes the AD823's main headphone weakness with about 2.5x the linear output current, and adds lower noise, higher slew and lower closed-loop Zout. The praised AD823 sound comes from the original CB part, mostly the PDIP AD823AN/ANZ, and should not be assumed to carry over.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium - same dual SOIC pinout and 3-36 V supply, but there is no DIP version, so DIP users need an adapter. Compensation and capacitive-load behaviour differ, input CM abs max is ±VS ± 0.7 V, and Rev. B warns of overheating at a 30 V supply.
silicon_changes.verification: Not re-searched: this is a high-confidence, data-sheet-backed entry that is not in the sweep. Classified as renumbering-or-successor rather than a same-number die redesign because the AD823A has distinct order codes (AD823AARZ/AARMZ).

counterfeit_notes: No AD823-specific counterfeit reports were found; forums were not searched for this. Soomal notes that the Graham Slee SOLO SRG II had its op-amp marking sanded off, which is not an AD823 counterfeit report. The following are inferences. (1) Leaded AD823AN appears to have been discontinued (PDN 10_0081, c. 2010) and is absent from the Rev. E ordering guide, so 'AD823AN' DIPs with recent date codes deserve scrutiny. (2) The AD823A exists only in SOIC/MSOP, so an 'AD823A' DIP is either a loosely described AD823AN/ANZ or a fake. (3) Listings confuse the original AD823AR/ARZ (A grade) with the 2012 AD823AARZ die; check the full order code and the datasheet number (D00901 vs D09439). (4) Genuine stock made after PCN 26_0029 (2026) comes from a different fab, so small differences between old and new genuine parts do not by themselves indicate fakes. Buy from authorized distributors.

open_questions: PCN 26_0029: issue date, implementation date, date-code or lot identification, the previous fab, whether the reel variants (-RL/-R7) and AD823A parts are included, and whether the die layout changes. Only search-result summaries were seen.

PDN 10_0081 Rev. B and PDN 16_0062: exact discontinued order codes, replacements and last-time-buy dates were read from search summaries only. The inferred mapping is AD823AN to AD823ANZ, and AD823AR/-REEL/-REEL7 to AD823ARZ/-RL/-R7.

No copies were confirmed of AD823 Rev. 0 (5/95), B (2/07), C (5/10) or D (6/10), or of AD823A Rev. A (5/12). The datasheetq '2007' entry and the datasheet4u/datasheetcatalog copies are candidates that have not been checked.
Lifecycle status of AD823AARZ/AARMZ is unverified; AD823ANZ and AD823ARZ are presumed active because they appear in a 2026 PCN.
Does ADI officially position the AD823A as the AD823's replacement?
Top-marking differences between AD823 SOIC and AD823A SOIC are unknown.
The Hidizs AP100's use of the AD823 (filter or headphone driver) is unresolved.
The Head-Fi threads (242125, 870832) and the diyAudio AD823-vs-OPA2132 thread were not read.
The AD823 Theory of Operation quotes a '1 mV maximum' offset, while Table 1 gives 0.8 mV max at 5 V (a minor inconsistency in Rev. A and Rev. E).

claims_confirmed: The current ADI AD823 datasheet URL serves 'Dual, 16 MHz, Rail-to-Rail FET Input Amplifier Data Sheet AD823 Rev. E' (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/AD823.pdf).
The front-page specs -108 dB THD at 20 kHz, 22 V/µs slew and 2.6 mA per amplifier are confirmed (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/ad823.pdf).
The Futurlec copy is Rev. A (https://futurlec.com/Datasheet/AnalogDevices/AD823AN.pdf).

The AD823A datasheet is titled 'Wide Supply Dual, 17 MHz, Rail-to-Rail FET Input Amplifier' at the vendor URL (https://www.analog.com/media/en/technical-documentation/data-sheets/AD823A.pdf) and is Revision B (https://www.radiolocman.com/datasheet/pdf.html?di=171865).

PCN 26_0029 leverages the existing qualified process at ADI's Camas, WA fab, with no expected fit/form/function/reliability impact (https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/8933/ADI_PCN_26_0029_Rev_-_Form.pdf).
AD823ANZ and AD823ARZ are listed in PCN 26_0029, per the search summary (https://www.farnell.com/datasheets/4778405.pdf).

PDN 16_0062 and PDN 10_0081 Rev. B reference AD823 order codes with replacements (https://media.digikey.com/pdf/PCNs/Analog%20Devices/ADI_PDN_16_0062_Rev_-_Form.pdf, https://www.analog.com/media/en/pcn/ADI_PDN_10_0081_Rev_B_Form.pdf).

Two search summaries call the Octopart copy Rev. B, and a '1995-2007' copyright was seen, but the PDF title shows no revision, so confidence is medium. No second-source vendors were found. No legacy analog.com paths (static/imported-files or UploadedFiles) for the AD823 came up, so none are given as archive seeds. The Wayback seeds given are the Reichelt, futurlec and Octopart copies and the ADI product pages.
